- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.17) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.22) and forecast is still trending up, adjust downward by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5 days.  
- If forecast spikes after a sharp drop (e.g., 2–3 days of decline followed by a spike), cap the spike at 10% above prior peak to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.00–0.17) and forecast is flat, add 1–2% upward bias to account for lagged market reaction.  
- If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days to reflect underestimation bias.
